title: Quantum solitons and their quantum walks in transmon arrays
authors: Ben Blain, Giampiero Marchegiani, Luigi Amico, Gianluigi Catelani
abstract: Superconducting qubits are artificial atoms whose spectra and interactions can be engineered through appropriate circuit design, a versatility that can be exploited for quantum simulation. We theoretically investigate a linear array of capacitively coupled transmons, effectively described by a Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian with attractive interaction. We revisit the discrete-soliton nature of the lowest-energy band of the spectrum, and identify spatially localized quantum solitons. The solitonic character of these states is revealed through their time evolution, which displays a quantum interference pattern, or quantum walk, highlighting their composite nature. We discuss protocols for preparing spatially localized quantum solitons that are compatible with current state-of-the-art tunable-transmon circuits. Our results demonstrate that superconducting circuits provide a promising and experimentally accessible platform for the investigation of quantum soliton physics.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates the existence and preparation of quantum solitons in arrays of superconducting transmon qubits modeled by an attractive Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian. By developing non-adiabatic state preparation protocols, the authors show that these localized soliton states can be reliably generated. The study further analyzes the unique quantum walk dynamics exhibited by these solitons compared to standard boson stacks.
main_problem: The study investigates quantum solitons and their associated quantum walks within superconducting transmon arrays, aiming to establish this platform for simulating complex many-body physics.
main_result: The research demonstrates that the system supports robust, spatially localized quantum soliton states whose preparation fidelity can be controlled via non-adiabatic protocols in superconducting circuits.
method: Theoretical analysis using the Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonian, involving numerical diagonalization, adiabatic/non-adiabatic state preparation protocols, and time evolution simulations to track quantum walk dynamics.
model_or_system: The physical system is a linear array of capacitively coupled transmons, modeled by an attractive Bose-Hubbard (BH) Hamiltonian. The analysis focuses on the emergence of a 'soliton band' in the energy spectrum when interactions are strong.
key_observables: Spatially localized quantum solitons, quantum interference patterns (quantum walk), correlation length ($\xi_C$), density decay length ($\xi_N$), and preparation fidelity ($I$).
important_parameters: Attractive interaction strength ($U < 0$), hopping parameter ($J$), particle number ($N=2, 3$), and pinning potential strengths ($\Delta\mu_6$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on approximations for effective hopping terms in the strongly attractive regime and assumes dynamic tunability of chemical potentials for state preparation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the BH spectrum showing a soliton band, compare density profiles for different soliton construction protocols, and track time evolution of occupation numbers and infidelity during quench dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework (BH model) to comparing multiple state preparation protocols (projected stack vs. single-stack), detailing optimal non-adiabatic quenching procedures, and finally analyzing the resulting quantum walk dynamics by comparing soliton evolution against standard boson stacks.
why_interesting: This work bridges superconducting circuit hardware with fundamental condensed matter physics concepts like solitons and quantum walks, providing a concrete roadmap for realizing complex many-body simulations on near-term quantum devices.
